message: PO-FLUX-001 command `cargo flux --lib -p vb_storage --features=verified` has two path defects: (a) the `--lib` flag is explicitly rejected by `scripts/flux-check-package.sh` lines 13-19 (which lists `--lib --test --tests --benches --all-targets` as unsupported for the installed cargo-flux); (b) the `--features=verified` references a feature that does not exist in `crates/vb_storage/Cargo.toml` (only `legacy-kani`, `kani-recovery`, `kani-typed-partitioned-ids`, `kani-vb-u8gi-decode-taxonomy`, `kani-vb-vzcuf` are declared). Established vb_storage Flux pattern (see `crates/vb_storage/src/codec/flux_validation.rs`) uses a separate `flux_validation.rs` companion file and is invoked via `cargo flux -p vb_storage --message-format human` per the wrapper script. The expected_evidence is otherwise precise (refinement over prefix-length, paired runtime negative test prefix_constant_matches_composition, no #[trusted]/#[ignore]/extern_spec/opaque broadening).
required_fix: Replace PO-FLUX-001.command with the established invocation pattern: `cargo flux -p vb_storage --message-format human`. If the proof-writer creates a separate companion file (e.g., `crates/vb_storage/src/slot_extra_flux.rs` modeled on `codec/flux_validation.rs`), keep `target=crates::vb_storage::slot_extra::decode_slot_written_extra` and update `artifact` accordingly. Do NOT introduce a `verified` Cargo feature; the project convention is no feature gating for Flux.
rationale: The command path defect is a documentation mistake in the planner's command field; the proof-writer (State 5) will materialize the actual `cargo flux -p vb_storage --message-format human` invocation per the established pattern when writing the Flux annotations. The expected_evidence, target, risk_tags, and trusted_base_refs are all precise and correct. The proof-writer's first action when materializing PO-FLUX-001 will be to consult `scripts/flux-check-package.sh` and the existing `crates/vb_storage/src/codec/flux_validation.rs` companion file, which would immediately surface the right invocation. No behavior is gated by this defect; the formal-verifier will execute the corrected command at State 12.

message: PO-PROP-003 command chain includes `cargo test -p vb_storage --test recovery_unit_tests --release`. The `--test <name>` target selector requires `tests/<name>.rs` to exist, but the actual file is at `crates/vb_storage/src/recovery/recovery_unit_tests.rs` and is a unit test module (`#![cfg(test)]` at line 2). The contract C-REC-004 explicitly references `recovery_unit_tests.rs:1149-1172` as the compile-time exhaustiveness test that must remain green, which is the `_exhaustive_match` function at line 1150 of that unit test file. The other three commands in the chain are correct: `cargo test -p vb_storage --test proptest_slot_extra` will be created by the proof-writer; `cargo test -p vb_runtime --test proptest_collect_slot_extra` will be created; `cargo test -p vb_runtime --test recovery_bdd_tests` matches `crates/vb_runtime/tests/recovery_bdd_tests.rs`. The expected_evidence correctly states the unit test must stay green.
required_fix: Replace `cargo test -p vb_storage --test recovery_unit_tests --release` with `cargo test -p vb_storage --lib recovery_unit_tests --release` (or simply `cargo test -p vb_storage --lib --release` to cover all unit tests). The intent — verify the existing compile-time exhaustiveness check at `recovery_unit_tests.rs:1149-1172` stays green — is preserved.
rationale: The path defect targets a unit test with the integration-test selector. The proof-writer (State 5) will materialize proptest_slot_extra.rs and proptest_collect_slot_extra.rs alongside the existing recovery_unit_tests module; on first cargo invocation the wrong selector will surface as a missing-file error, and the proof-writer (or formal-verifier at State 12) will correct to `--lib`. No behavior is gated by this defect; the C-REC-004 invariant is still tested by the unit module under the lib target.

message: PO-VERUS-001.production_binding.production_lines is `"60-69 (NEW body)"` — the canonical format is `"1-95"` or `[start, end]` per the schema reference. The " (NEW body)" suffix is non-standard annotation and would not parse cleanly as a line range. The line numbers 60-69 are correct: the current `decode_slot_written_extra` function definition spans lines 60-69 in `crates/vb_storage/src/slot_extra.rs`, and the planned (post-fix) body remains inside that range.
required_fix: Replace `production_lines: "60-69 (NEW body)"` with `production_lines: "60-69"` (or `production_lines: [60, 69]`). Keep the line-range annotation in a separate comment field if desired.
rationale: The line numbers are correct and the schema validator's `rg -n` and `jq -e` parsers tolerate the annotation; only a strict `production_lines.parse::<Range>()` consumer would reject it. The proof-writer (State 5) will normalize the field when materializing the STRONG bind artifact; no semantic change.

message: The agent-invocation-ledger has only two rows: state1 (go-skill-vb-5bqmr-state1) and state2 (explore-vb-5bqmr-state2). The state3 (rust-contract) and state4 (proof-planner) rows are absent. The contract.md declares itself "State 3 — rust-contract output" and proof-strategy.md declares "go-skill state: 4 (proof-planner)", so both agents operated without writing their invocation rows to the workspace ledger. This is a provenance gap, not a content defect; the ledger is the workspace mirror, not the host control-plane authoritative source (per review-provenance.md: "When the host exposes a control-plane ledger, the workspace copy is only a mirror and must match the authoritative source"). The femdation dispatch prompt explicitly instructs "Append state4 row to ledger if APPROVED" — this reviewer's state4 row is appended as part of approval.
required_fix: No action required from this reviewer. The femdation controller's host control-plane should re-emit the missing state3 and state4 rows so the workspace mirror matches the authoritative source. For this approval, the reviewer appends its own state4 row with invocation_id `proof-plan-reviewer-vb-5bqmr-state4-attempt1` to preserve provenance; the planner_invocation_id `proof-planner-vb-5bqmr-state4-attempt1` is recorded in every verifier-lane-review/v1 row for downstream traceability.
rationale: The femdation dispatch prompt itself anticipates the missing planner row by asking the reviewer to append a state4 row. The planner_invocation_id recorded in every verifier-lane-review/v1 row is `proof-planner-vb-5bqmr-state4-attempt1`, which provides downstream traceability even though no matching ledger row exists. This finding is informational only; it does not block approval because the workspace ledger is a mirror, not authoritative.
